title: Structured output contracts
summary: This intermediate guide shows practitioners how to represent a field with a fixed set of allowed values instead of using a placeholder string that cannot enforce those values.
prerequisites: A structured output contract containing a status field
A way to validate sample outputs against that contract

sections.title: Use enforceable alternatives
paragraphs: How should a status field allow only complete, needs-input, or blocked? In a JSON Schema contract, define those three strings as separate enum values. Do not encode them as the single string complete | needs-input | blocked.
A quoted sequence containing vertical bars is one JSON string. The bars do not declare alternatives. The enum keyword instead constrains an instance to equal one of the values in its array.

sections.title: Apply and review the correction
paragraphs: Step 1: Locate the rule for the status field and replace only the literal placeholder with the enum shown above. If the existing contract is not JSON Schema, do not paste this fragment into it; identify the contract's documented allowed-values mechanism before making the correction.

Step 2: Preserve the surrounding fields, wording, and contract structure. If the fragment cannot be inserted without changing unrelated material, stop and compare against the existing resource before proceeding.

Step 3: Test each allowed string and at least one unlisted string. If an allowed string is rejected or an unlisted string is accepted, confirm that the validator is applying the intended schema fragment and correct that connection before publishing.

The cited source that moved or passed its review cadence is UNKNOWN because the inspection did not identify it. What that source change affected is also UNKNOWN. The inspection independently establishes that the status example needs correction, but it does not establish a connection between that defect and a specific changed source.
sections.callout: Do not treat a source as reverified merely because its recorded date is no longer in the future. Verification requires checking the source.

sections.title: Expected result and verification
paragraphs: The expected result is a contract in which the status value accepts complete, needs-input, and blocked as three distinct alternatives rather than displaying them as one placeholder string.

Verify the result by validating each of the three listed strings separately. Then validate an unlisted string. Success requires all three listed values to pass and the unlisted value to fail. If that evidence is not produced, inspect whether the status rule is being applied at the correct location in the surrounding contract and repeat the checks.
